findings.title: Global canManage() grants manage on VIEW
findings.body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70, canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), identical to canView(). This lets an admin with only VIEW on the all-groups resource pass requireManage(), e.g. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup which requires global manage. Consequence is privilege escalation: read-only group viewers can create top-level groups. Fix is to check only MANAGE for global manage, matching per-group canManage(group) which correctly checks only MANAGE.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource UUID instead of group ID
findings.body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122-123, findByType iterates group resources but calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId()) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). Per AdminPermissionsSchema group resources are named by groupId (resolveGroup returns groupId) while getId() is the internal authz UUID, so findByName lookup misses and the granted set contains authz UUIDs not group IDs. UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource then filter user searches and counts by UserModel.GROUPS with bogus IDs, returning empty or wrong user sets and breaking pagination.

findings.title: Per-object group resources created without type breaks findByType
findings.body: In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:121, getOrCreateResource creates a resource with resourceStore.create(server, name, clientId) and updates scopes but never calls setType(resourceType), while init() for aggregate resources does setType(type). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission relies on resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Since per-group resources have null type they are never found, the method always returns empty, disabling store-level filtering of users by view-members and forcing full scans with in-memory filtering and incorrect first/max pagination.

findings.title: V2 group management methods throw breaking deletion
findings.body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:174, setPermissionsEnabled (and isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, view/manage permission accessors) throw UnsupportedOperationException. AdminPermissions.registerListener calls management().groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group,false) on GroupRemovedEvent, and GroupResource management/permissions endpoints call the same methods. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, deleting any group aborts the transaction with 500 and leaks authz resources, and the management endpoints always fail.

findings.title: Existing realms never get Groups resource and scopes
findings.body: In server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:250, init() returns early if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. Existing realms that already have the admin-permissions client (with only Users/Clients) therefore never get the new Groups aggregate resource nor the new scopes manage-members/view-members/manage-membership. Later getOrCreateResource for Groups then throws ModelException No scopes found because scopeStore.findByName returns null, breaking group permission creation on upgrade.

findings.title: Missing null-check for all-groups fallback causes NPE
findings.body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:147, hasPermission falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource for Groups when no per-group resource exists, then immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and new ResourcePermission(resource,...) without checking for null. getResourceTypeResource explicitly can return null (unsupported schema, missing type, missing resource). Consequence is NullPointerException during any group permission check when the aggregate Groups resource is absent, e.g. upgraded realms or misconfigured servers.

findings.title: Impersonation with requester evaluates wrong identity
findings.body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/UserPermissionsV2.java:71, canImpersonate(user, requester) builds DefaultEvaluationContext with new UserModelIdentity(root.realm, user) when requester != null, then evaluates IMPERSONATE on the target user's resource with that context. That evaluates as the target user, not the admin attempting impersonation (plus kc.client.id claim). Legitimate admin impersonation with a requesting client will fail policy checks for the admin and may incorrectly succeed/deny based on target attributes. Correct context should use the admin identity with the client-id claim, as V1 does for admin checks.

findings.title: Removed global-view short-circuit causes per-group evaluations
findings.body: In services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupsResource.java:113 (and GroupResource.java:179), the filter was changed from cached canViewGlobal || canView(g) to stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView). For V2, global VIEW via all-groups permission now requires a full authz evaluation per group instead of one cached evaluation with short-circuit, turning group listing into O(N) policy evaluations. Consequence is severe latency on realms with many groups for admins with all-groups access.
